title: Workspace route
description: One role of one project on one machine: where its source is read from. Machine-local by law — this schema is shared, the files it validates never are.

$schema.description: Optional. A route is validated by being handed to the validator, not by carrying a pointer to it.

project.description: User-declared. Never inferred from a folder name — that is the WORKSPACE-1 failure.

role.description: `fe`, `be`, a legacy role, or a role of the tree's own tooling such as `console`.

source.description: Where the trust tree is, on this machine.

repository.description: The checkout this role reads. The route DESCRIBES it and never mirrors it.

diskPath.description: Read directly. A mirror, mount or cached copy is WORKSPACE-3.

gitRepository.description: The origin remote — the one field that identifies the repository rather than this machine.

head.description: Evidence of freshness, not a pin. A head that no longer belongs to the checkout makes the route stale — WORKSPACE-5 — and stale is a different verdict from absent.

context.description: What the role must read before it can answer anything.

contract.description: The domain contract. `null` is legitimate for a backend or tooling role. For a frontend role it is a finding, not a shape: a monorepo keeps its registry somewhere a one-app convention does not look.

contractSource.description: How that path was chosen — `declared:…` or `discovered:…`. A reviewer is owed this when the path turns out wrong.

manifests.description: Package or workspace manifests, used to choose commands.

grammar.description: Explicit product-family grammar id. Never inferred from project or repository identity.

grammarProfile.description: Explicit owner profile inside the selected grammar. Must be null when grammar is null.

updatedAt.description: When setup last verified this route, not when it was written.

absolutePath.description: Absolute, and therefore machine-local. This is the one place in the tree's world where an absolute path is correct — and the reason a route file is never committed into the tree.
